Should the mounting bolts for the pump become loose the pump could bounce on the frame at each compression stroke as additional torque is applied to the drive belt causing vibration and noise. Tighten the mounting bolts to correct the problem...

There are three bearings in the typical pneumatic pump, any of which will become noisy when worn. Replacement of the defective bearings is the only fix for the problem. Defective wrist pin bearings or rod bearings make a "knocking" sound, 2 per revolution. Defective main bearings "knock" once at each revolution......on.ce at each revolution.on.....

Noise caused by low oil in the crankcase is an indication that moving parts are working without lubrication, a situation that will cause permanent damage. Check the oil at intervals recommended by the manufacturer. Use only the recommended lubricant...c

Low oil in a pump crankcase can cause enough damage to require a full rebuild of the pump. Since the fluid medium in a pneumatic system is a gas, the crankcase oil provides lubrication to all internal moving parts...

A loose pulley can rotate on the shaft against the keeper or set screw causing a "banging" on the compression stroke. Tightening the set screw will usually correct the problem if caught early. Damage to the pulley or the pump shaft can result if repairs are postponed...
Noisy operation has several causes: ose pulley. Low oil in the crankcase. Worn bearings. Loose pump mounting. Noisy check valve..ng. Noisy check valve..ve.

The piston rings are also a cause of low compression. Air will slip past the ring during the compression stroke into the crankcase, preventing maximum pressure build up. Replacement of the rings is usually all that is required, but be sure to follow the manufacturer's recommendations...

One cause for low compression is a bad valve. A defective valve will prevent the pressure from building as it will constantly leak. A tear down and rebuild is required. The valves are usually easy to replace as most manufactures recommend replacement at preset times to ensure optimum performance...

A pump with low compression will run longer than usual before shutting off, or run continuously, never shutting off as pressure does not reach the shut off point. Low compression is rarely something that happens quickly. As the moving parts begin to wear the efficiency of the pump slowly diminishes until the pump is no longer capable of producing adequate pressure.....

Low discharge output pressure can be caused by low compression. When everything else checks OK, low compression must be considered. If the pump has been neglected, or has been in service for a long time, it's probably time for a pump tear down and rebuild......
Low discharge output pressure can also be causd by air intake restrictions. Remove the air filter and check for restored performance. Replace the air filter if performance improves.

Low discharge output pressure can cause discharge leaks or obstructions. Listen and look for air leaks or physical damage in the discharge plumbing. Review any recent repairs to the system in search of obstructions. Check any hoses for kinks, sharp bends, and cuts. Look for blown gaskets.

Excessive air demand can be caused by too many tools in use at the same time. Review the usage to determine if the system is still capable of handling the air volume and pressure demand. A larger system may be required.uired.. larger system may be required.ed...

Large industrial applications may cascade several stages and may also liquid cool the assembly to absorb heat. It is also common for the subsequent stage(s) to be physically smaller than the first stage...

You'll note the compressed heated air from the first stage is also the suction air for the second stage. To keep the temperature of the air at a reasonable level the air is cooled using a long inner-connecting line with cooling fins...

Pump cylinders are also cascaded, or placed in series, when constant high pressure requirements are more important than flow volume. In a multiple stage cascade pump the discharge of the first cylinder is connected to the suction of the next cylinder in line. The final stage in line is the pump discharge...

An alternative to the double-action pump is the dual stage pump using two cylinders with common suction and discharge ports. Using a double-action or dual stage pump increases the amount of airflow available, measured in cubic feet per minute, CFM...

Double-action pumps can pump twice as much air as single-action pumps. Double-action pumps are always single cylinder pumps. They require extra linkages to ensure the piston rod is kept in exact position throughout travel to ensure adequate sealing around the piston rod...

A double-action pump is drawing in air and compressing/discharging air almost throughout the reciprocating process. Only at the extreme ends of piston travel does airflow cease. The pump uses two suction and two discharge valves. Their action alternates with the piston travel...

The action of compressing the air causes the air to heat up. Cooling fins are usually on the outside of the cylinder to help dissipate the heat. The technician troubleshooting the system should be aware a burn hazard is present and plan accordingly.y.

After the piston bottoms out in the cylinder it begins the upstroke. The air is compressed as the volume gets smaller. When the pressure inside the cylinder exceeds the pressure at the other side of the discharge valve, the discharge valve opens and the air is pressed out of the cylinder and into the pneumatic system.....

The single-action piston pump most resembles the piston and cylinder in a car, motorcycle, or lawnmower engine. During the down stroke the vacuum created by the expanding volume opens the suction valve, allowing air into the cylinder as the pressure equalizes..
The piston pump is the standard pump used in pneumatic systems. Piston pumps may be single-action, double-action, or multi-stage with two or more cylinders.
The piston pump used on an air compressor relies on the reciprocating, or back and forth, motion of a piston to pressurize the gas.

Throughout this lesson air will be used as the fluid medium in pneumatic systems. While used in most cases, air is not the only fluid medium used in pneumatic systems. In industrial applications with possible fire hazards nitrogen is sometimes used to decrease the fire hazard....

There are several different types of pumps used in pneumatic systems. The piston pump is used in most applications. The piston pump, motor, receiver (storage tank) and pressure switch make up an assembly commonly known as the air compressor...

Gases, though, can be compressed. The pressure is maintained in the system by the storage tank, or receiver, and the expansion of the gas as it flows provides the energy for the system. The pump in a pneumatic system is started and stopped as needed by a pressure switch...

In the typical application the hydraulic system the pump runs continuously with a bypass relief valve maintaining fluid flow through the pump when the pressure is not used by an actuator in the system. The liquid cannot be compressed and the system pressure must come from the pump...

The use of a gas as the fluid medium also changes the overall design of a pneumatic system as compared to a hydraulic system. Both systems must sustain pressure but the compressibility of the medium changes the way each system operates...
The use of a gas as the fluid medium prohibits the pump lubrication and cooling action provided by the fluid in a hydraulic system. This greatly changes the demands and design of the pump used...

Reciprocating pumps are preferred over rotary pumps in pneumatic systems as they produce higher pressures using a gas, usually air, as the fluid medium. There is also little chance of fluid seepage from the discharge outlet of the pump to the suction inlet due to the construction of the pump...

Positive displacement pumps are self-priming and provide high output pressure. There are two categories of positive displacement pumps, the reciprocating and the rotary. Pneumatic systems usually are powered by a reciprocating pump...

Pumps used in pneumatic systems are also positive displacement pumps.

As a system ages it's efficiency diminishes somewhat with time due to wear of moving components and corrosion buildup. If the system was marginal when first installed it will be difficult to keep optimum performance as the system ages...

Misalignment of the components could put additional strain on the equipment. The mechanical alignment between the prime mover and the pump is the final suspect. But, sloppy alignment of hose fittings and other mechanical connections in the system should also be checked...

An obstruction in the discharge circuit can increase pressure in the system and reduce fluid flow causing the fluid to overheat. Check any valves inline with the discharge to ensure they are not stuck. It may also be necessary to check the system for obstructions...
If the pump has recently been serviced the pump packing or seals may be too tight. It may be necessary to dismantle the pump and check the packing and/or seals.

As with many other symptoms, first check the hydraulic fluid in the reservoir. If the fluid viscosity has increased the additional fluid viscosity weight will increase the load on the pump, and therefore, the prime mover. When in doubt, change the fluid...

Additional strain on the pump is passed onto the prime mover. The symptoms of pulling too much power include:ripping circuit breakers, overheating of the prime mover, reduced system performance, and high fluid temperature..

The best cure for both corrosion and contamination is the periodic replacement of the hydraulic fluid. Consult the manufacturer for recommended fluid replacement intervals.

Contamination of the fluid in a hydraulic system can wreck havoc. Most contamination is water condensed into the fluid over time. Water can foam, reducing both the viscosity of the fluid and the fluid lubrication properties. In systems used periodically the water can collect in areas causing corrosion...
Corrosion of components can also accelerate pump wear. Corrosion in the system increases the load on the pump causing early wear and eventual reduction of performance.

Mechanically, a dry running pump or one that takes a long time to prime can wear at a greater than expected rate. Mechanical strain caused by pump casing misalignment can twist the pump internals over time causing premature wear. Verify the pump installation is optimum and component alignment is accurate after rebuild or replacement.....

DEFINITION
VISCOSITY - A measure of a fluid's resistance to flow. The viscosity of a fluid usually varies with temperature; less viscous as the temperature rises and more viscous with decreasing temperature.
DEFINITION
CAVITATION - The sudden formation and collapse of low-pressure bubbles in a flowing liquid in regions of very low pressure, often damaging impellers and pumps.

A noisy pump can also be caused by cavitation brought on by old hydraulic fluid or fluid of the wrong viscosity. When in doubt, change the fluid. Prolonged cavitation shortens the life of the pump as much as running a pump dry.
Check the pump for foreign items internally. Also look for bad bearings, bent shafts, misalignment of parts, or a noisy relief valve.

Valve related problems could reduce the fluid output also. Misadjusted or jammed relief or bypass valves, or partially closed suction or discharge valves will reduce the fluid flow in a hydraulic system...

Pump related problems include the loss of pump prime and a pump running backwards. Loss of prime can be caused by a suction air leak or bad pump packing, seals, or gaskets. If it is discovered a pump is rotating in reverse, check the motor connected to the pump...
Valve related problems can be caused by misadjusted or jammed relief or bypass valves, or closed suction or discharge valves.

Fluid related problems are quickly resolved. First check the reservoir and ensure there is sufficient fluid available. Also check to ensure the pick up tube is below the fluid level, and the strainer or filter at the end of the pickup tube, if equipped, is not clogged. Finally, verify the proper fluid is being used...

The first step in troubleshooting a suspected pump is the first observe the hydraulic system. Look for obvious signs of problems such as leaks, broken pipes, tubing, or hoses, and missing hydraulic components...

The technician should be aware of the normal output pressure of the pump, the motion of the actuators in the system, the proper valve operation, and the condition of the reservoir and the other devices in the system...

In hydraulic system failures one of the most suspected causes of reduced or loss of operation is the pump. However, before jumping right in to dismantling the pump, the technician should be aware and familiar with the normal operation of the hydraulic system...

It's easy to see the wear factor could be greater with the vane pump than with other rotary pumps due to the required seal at the outer edge of the vane. Most manufacturers provide replacement vanes for pump repair, making restoration to service easier than other types of pumps...
The sliding vane pump is the best positive displacement rotary pump for self-priming. Centrifugal force caused by the rotation keeps the vanes against the outer wall of the eccentric pump housing..
Both rotors of the lobe pump are driven through external timing geared configurations.

The lobe pump is similar to the external gear pump but it uses two or three lobes instead of gears. Three lobe pumps produce a smoother pressured output than two lobe pumps. Lobe pumps also have less internal wear than gear pumps, and therefore, should last longer in a given application...
The external gear pump uses two gears of equal size. Notice the rotation direction of the gears.

The rotor of the internal gear pump is inside the idler gear and turns at a faster speed than the idler due to the size difference. The gears are fully meshed at only one point of the rotation. The crescent-shaped divider between the gears prevents backflow from the discharge port to the suction port...

Gear pumps operate using a pair of gears. One gear is driven by the prime mover, the rotor gear, and the second gear is driven by the rotor, the idler gear. The un-meshing actions of the gear teeth create the vacuum into which the fluid flows. Fluid is then accelerated out of the pump through the discharge port...
The most popular types of rotary pumps used in hydraulic systems are the gear pump, the lobe pump, and the vane pump.

Most applications include a pressure released bypass valve, as the pump will not last long working against a closed discharge port. Hydraulic fluid would overheat and begin loosing viscosity quickly if fluid flow was not maintained through the pump. This would reduce the life of the pump...

Rotary pumps use the vacuum created by an expanding volume to induce fluid flow, making them self-priming. Pressure is then created through the rotational operation. Rotary pumps rely on the pumped fluid to provide the lubrication and cooling needed for proper operation and long life...

Positive displacement pumps are self-priming and provide high output pressure. There are two categories of positive displacement pumps, the reciprocating and the rotary. Hydraulic systems usually are powered by a rotary pump..

Pumps used in hydraulic systems are positive displacement pumps.
